expectations.text: The reply says that in Sweden the selection follows the LAS order by length of service, unless a collective agreement or a list agreed with the union says otherwise, and that the employer may exempt up to three employees.
expectations.evidence: Reply: "In Sweden the Employment Protection Act (LAS) decides who stays: length of service within each priority group, unless you agree a different order with the union, plus up to three exemptions." Document section 5 adds the priority group per Malmö unit and agreement area, the age tie-break and "up to three people of particular importance to continued operations".

expectations.text: The reply says the employer must negotiate with the union under the Co-determination Act (MBL) before deciding.
expectations.evidence: Reply: "Negotiate with the union under MBL before deciding, with the real numbers and alternatives." Document: "Start MBL negotiations before any decision" and "draft for negotiation with the union (MBL §11). Nothing is decided yet."

expectations.text: The reply rejects selecting people by tickets resolved or CSAT as the method, and explains why (the law and the metric's flaws).
expectations.evidence: Reply: "Don't select on tickets resolved and CSAT. In Sweden the Employment Protection Act (LAS) decides who stays ... A ticket-and-CSAT ranking would be hard to defend, and with AI taking the easy tickets it marks down the agents handling the hardest cases." Document: "people get very different case mixes, and CSAT mostly reflects the customer's issue." Both the law and the metric's flaws are covered.

expectations.text: The reply mentions the nine-month re-employment priority and support through a job security council or transition study support.
expectations.evidence: Reply: "Support from the day of notice: job security council, one to six months' notice, nine months' rehiring priority." Document adds TRR, or Kammarkollegiet's basic support if there is no collective agreement, and the 12-months-in-three-years condition.

expectations.text: The reply first checks the cut itself: whether people could be redeployed to other work (for example complex cases or new services) instead of nine dismissals.
expectations.evidence: The first bullet is "Check the 9 first: track escalations, reopens and CSAT on AI-handled contacts for a few weeks." Then: "Avoid dismissals where you can: vacancies, redeployment (a legal duty), escalation and AI-quality roles, ending temp work, attrition, voluntary packages." Document: "If the data supports fewer than 9 reductions, the number changes" and "Create roles for the new work: escalation specialists, knowledge-base upkeep, AI quality review."

expectations.text: The reply stays short (under about 300 words) and opens with the answer.

factual_errors.evidence: Checked and correct: LAS §22 priority group per operating unit and collective agreement area, order by total length of employment with the older employee taking priority on a tie, up to three exemptions with no further exemptions for notices within three months (English translation of §22). Also correct: the Arbetsförmedlingen notice at least two months before the first affected person's last day for up to 25 people (arbetsformedlingen.se), notice of 1-6 months (LAS §11), nine months' priority for people with more than 12 months in three years, TRR, and Kammarkollegiet's basic support under Lag 2022:850 for employers without a collective agreement. Klarna's 2025 move back to human agents after lower quality matches Bloomberg and Entrepreneur reporting. One ambiguity, not an error: 'with equal service, the older employee goes first' means first in the priority order (kept), but in a layoff context 'goes' could be misread as 'leaves'.

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of a skill, reference files, 'cost ladder' or 'rungs'. 'skills' appears only as employee skills ('documented skills').

owns_result.evidence: The prompt describes a planned reduction, not a bad outcome that leadership caused.

best_insight.value: The handed-over document is a negotiation-ready draft. It sets out the operative LAS §22 mechanics (priority group per Malmö unit and agreement area, age tie-break, the three-month bar on further exemptions), the varsel timing from the first last day, a Kammarkollegiet fallback if there is no collective agreement, and linked sources, so counsel and the union can check it line by line.

suggestions.reason: All four samples pass all six assertions, so the set does not separate them. The differences sit in things no assertion checks: the Arbetsförmedlingen notice (two months before the first last day for 5-25 people), defining the remaining roles and their qualification needs before anyone is assessed, ruling out leave, sickness and part-time as factors, and cutting work along with roles.

suggestions.assertion: The reply stays short (under about 300 words) and opens with the answer.
suggestions.reason: Every reply is 258-270 words, so 'under about 300' doesn't discriminate. It also ignores that one sample adds a 622-word document after the user said 'Keep it short'. Consider an assertion on whether the whole hand-over respects that request, or a tighter cap.

suggestions.assertion: The reply first checks the cut itself: whether people could be redeployed to other work (for example complex cases or new services) instead of nine dismissals.
suggestions.reason: This is a compound check (question the 9, then redeploy to new work), and all samples pass it easily. A sharper version would ask the reply to test the cut against measured AI quality (reopens, escalations), not vendor deflection figures, before anyone is selected.

Consider an assertion that the reply turns HR's aim into something lawful, such as a union-agreed list on objective, role-based criteria fixed before scoring, instead of only rejecting it. Only some samples do this explicitly.

eval_feedback.overall: Passes all six. It is the most complete and legally precise sample, with a sourced draft document on top of a 258-word reply. The extra document stretches 'Keep it short', and 'the older employee goes first' is ambiguous wording.
